newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's BUX falls amid bearish Central Euro trend.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's BUX falls amid bearish Central Euro trend.

text.p: The Hungarian share market moved in concert with other central European bourses and drifted lower and analysts said they did not see any strong direction for the Budapest bourse in the short term.
The BUX index finished at a preliminary 5,795.24 points, down 52.96.
"We still see it (the market) trading sideways, we still think it is really too expensive," said Frances Cloud of Nomura Equity Research in London.
"But there's very little sign of people actively selling, so we think it is going to continue to move up a little bit one day, down little bit the next, with no particular trend."
On Thursday nine shares ended higher, 25 lower and two closed unchanged.
The losers included oil company Magyar Olaj- es Gazipari Rt (MOL) and pharmaceuticals Richter Gedeon Rt.
MOL gave up 45 forints to end at 3,255, after the global coordinators in its private placement called an overallotment option for 2.5 percent of MOL shares.

Richter lost 215 forints to end at 14,240 forints, amid speculations about the pricing in the second phase of its privatisation later on Thursday. One trader explained Richter's fall by the fact that certain investors began to unload the paper.
Traders said the market's fall on Thursday was in line with the trend in other central European markets -- Warsaw and Prague -- and was due to profit-taking.
"Investors are locking in profits, this is true for almost all stocks," said Peter Tolgyesi of Buda-Cash Brokerhaz.
While some investors decided to lock in profits, the market apparently lacked new buyers, he said.
"For the time being the inflow of funds into the Hungarian market is not strong enough to keep prices level," said Tolgyesi, adding "this was valid for central European bourses too, today."
Should prices lose further ground, lower levels might offer new buying opportunities, traders said.
On Thursday, OTP Securities initiated an analysis on Danubius Hotels with "hold" and another on chemicals Tiszai Vegyi Kombinat (TVK) with "buy".
They closed at 5,325 forints, down 175 and at 2,625 forints, down 60, respectively.
